title: XERODERMA PIGMENTOSUM, VARIANT TYPE
alt_titles: XERODERMA PIGMENTOSUM WITH NORMAL DNA REPAIR RATES

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that the variant type of xeroderma pigmentosum (XPV) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding DNA polymerase eta (POLH; 603968) on chromosome 6p21.

checks.claim: The variant type of xeroderma pigmentosum (XPV) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding DNA polymerase eta (POLH).
checks.evidence_quote: We found that all XP-V cells examined carry mutations in their DNA polymerase eta gene.
checks.explanation: The abstract links XPV to mutations in the pol eta gene. It does not say whether they are homozygous or compound heterozygous, and it states causation cautiously ('could be the XPV gene product').

checks.claim: The POLH gene, encoding DNA polymerase eta, is located on chromosome 6p21.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not give a chromosomal location for the gene.

paragraphs.text: Xeroderma pigmentosum variant type (XPV) is an autosomal recessive disorder of sun sensitivity. Patients develop pigmentary changes in sun-exposed skin and have a much higher risk of cutaneous malignancies. Clinically it resembles classical xeroderma pigmentosum, but onset is usually milder and later, and neurologic abnormalities are generally absent. Unlike cells from the classical XP complementation groups, XPV cells have normal nucleotide excision repair. Their defect is in replicating past UV-induced DNA damage (translesion synthesis), which is caused by loss of DNA polymerase eta.

checks.claim: Xeroderma pigmentosum variant type (XPV) is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Xeroderma pigmentosum (XP) is an autosomal recessive disease characterized by a high incidence of skin cancers.
checks.explanation: The abstract calls XP in general autosomal recessive. It does not say this specifically about the variant form.

checks.claim: Xeroderma pigmentosum variant type (XPV) is a disorder of sun sensitivity.
checks.evidence_quote: Patients with xeroderma pigmentosum variant show clinical photosensitivity
checks.explanation: Photosensitivity equals sun sensitivity.

checks.claim: Patients with XPV develop pigmentary changes in sun-exposed skin.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 7 cited papers. The abstract does not mention pigmentary changes.

checks.claim: Patients with XPV have a much higher risk of cutaneous malignancies.
checks.evidence_quote: The correlation between this defect and high levels of actinic carcinogenesis in these patients points to an important role for perturbations in DNA replication in human carcinogenesis.
checks.explanation: High levels of actinic (sun-induced) carcinogenesis in XP variant patients.

checks.claim: XPV clinically resembles classical xeroderma pigmentosum.
checks.evidence_quote: The "pigmented xerodermoid" was previously defined on the basis of mild clinical symptoms that suggested it might be similar to but distinct from xeroderma pigmentosum (XP).
checks.explanation: Abstract says the pigmented xerodermoid (shown equivalent to XP variant) was clinically similar to XP; it does not directly describe XPV's clinical resemblance in detail.

checks.claim: The onset of XPV is usually milder and later than that of classical xeroderma pigmentosum.
checks.evidence_quote: The "pigmented xerodermoid" was previously defined on the basis of mild clinical symptoms
checks.explanation: Milder symptoms are mentioned for the pigmented xerodermoid (equated with XPV), but later onset is not stated.

checks.claim: Neurologic abnormalities are generally absent in XPV.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The abstract does not discuss neurologic abnormalities.

checks.claim: Unlike cells from the classical XP complementation groups, XPV cells have normal nucleotide excision repair.
checks.evidence_quote: There is, however, one class of these patients whose cells are completely normal in this excision repair process.
checks.explanation: Most XP cells are defective in excision repair; the variant class is normal.

checks.claim: The defect in XPV cells is in replicating past UV-induced DNA damage (translesion synthesis).
checks.evidence_quote: XP-V cells carry out normal nucleotide-excision repair processes but are defective in their replication of ultraviolet-damaged DNA.
checks.explanation: Stated directly; the abstract also mentions trans-lesion DNA synthesis.

checks.claim: The translesion synthesis defect in XPV cells is caused by loss of DNA polymerase eta.
checks.evidence_quote: DNA polymerase eta (poleta) performs translesion synthesis past ultraviolet (UV) photoproducts and is deficient in cancer-prone xeroderma pigmentosum variant (XP-V) syndrome.
checks.explanation: Directly stated.

paragraphs.text: Affected individuals have sun sensitivity with freckle-like pigmentation and other actinic changes of exposed skin. They develop basal cell carcinomas, squamous cell carcinomas and melanomas of sun-exposed sites. Skin cancers often appear later than in classical XP, and some patients are not diagnosed until adulthood. Neurologic degeneration, a feature of some classical XP groups, is not a feature of XPV.

checks.claim: Individuals with XPV have sun sensitivity.
checks.evidence_quote: Patients with xeroderma pigmentosum variant show clinical photosensitivity
checks.explanation: Photosensitivity equals sun sensitivity.

checks.claim: Individuals with XPV have freckle-like pigmentation and other actinic changes of exposed skin.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 7 cited papers. The abstract does not mention freckle-like pigmentation or actinic changes.

checks.claim: Individuals with XPV develop basal cell carcinomas of sun-exposed sites.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 6 cited papers. The abstract mentions only 'skin neoplasias'; basal cell carcinoma is not specified.

checks.claim: Individuals with XPV develop squamous cell carcinomas of sun-exposed sites.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 6 cited papers. The abstract mentions only 'skin neoplasias'; squamous cell carcinoma is not specified.

checks.claim: Individuals with XPV develop melanomas of sun-exposed sites.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 6 cited papers. The abstract mentions only 'skin neoplasias'; melanoma is not specified.

checks.claim: Skin cancers in XPV often appear later than in classical xeroderma pigmentosum.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The abstract does not discuss the timing of skin cancers relative to classical XP.

checks.claim: Some patients with XPV are not diagnosed until adulthood.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The abstract does not mention age at diagnosis.

checks.claim: Neurologic degeneration is a feature of some classical xeroderma pigmentosum groups.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. Neurologic degeneration not mentioned.

checks.claim: Neurologic degeneration is not a feature of XPV.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 6 cited papers. The abstract does not mention neurologic degeneration.

paragraphs.text: Cleaver (1972) described patients with clinical xeroderma pigmentosum whose cells showed normal levels of UV-induced unscheduled DNA synthesis. This set them apart from the excision-deficient forms of XP.

checks.claim: Cleaver (1972) described patients with clinical xeroderma pigmentosum whose cells showed normal levels of UV-induced unscheduled DNA synthesis.
checks.evidence_quote: Xeroderma pigmentosum: variants with normal DNA repair and normal sensitivity to ultraviolet light.
checks.explanation: The title reports normal DNA repair in XP variants. The specific measure, UV-induced unscheduled DNA synthesis, would be in the full text, which was not supplied.

checks.claim: The normal UV-induced unscheduled DNA synthesis in cells from the patients described by Cleaver (1972) set them apart from the excision-deficient forms of xeroderma pigmentosum.
checks.evidence_quote: Xeroderma pigmentosum: variants with normal DNA repair and normal sensitivity to ultraviolet light.
checks.explanation: Normal DNA repair implies these patients differ from repair-deficient XP. The title does not mention unscheduled DNA synthesis or the excision-deficient forms explicitly.

paragraphs.text: Lehmann et al. (1975) found that XP variant cells were defective in postreplication repair. After UV irradiation, the cells were abnormally slow to convert newly synthesized low-molecular-weight DNA into high-molecular-weight DNA. Caffeine made this defect worse. Increased sensitivity of UV-irradiated variant cells to caffeine was later used as a laboratory diagnostic feature.

checks.claim: Lehmann et al. (1975) found that XP variant cells were defective in postreplication repair.
checks.evidence_quote: Xeroderma pigmentosum cells with normal levels of excision repair have a defect in DNA synthesis after UV-irradiation.
checks.explanation: The paper describes a defect in DNA synthesis after UV, which amounts to postreplication repair, but the abstract does not use the term 'postreplication repair'.

checks.claim: After UV irradiation, XP variant cells were abnormally slow to convert newly synthesized low-molecular-weight DNA into high-molecular-weight DNA.
checks.evidence_quote: The time taken to convert initially low-molecular-weight DNA synthesized in UV-irradiated cells into high-molecular-weight DNA similar in size to that in untreated cells is much greater in these variants than in normal cells.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Caffeine made the postreplication repair defect of XP variant cells worse.
checks.evidence_quote: Furthermore, this slow conversion of low to high-molecular-weight newly synthesized DNA is drastically inhibited by caffeine, which has no effect in normal cells.
checks.explanation: Caffeine inhibits the conversion, which makes the defect worse.

checks.claim: Increased sensitivity of UV-irradiated XP variant cells to caffeine was later used as a laboratory diagnostic feature.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention later use of caffeine sensitivity as a diagnostic test.

paragraphs.text: XPV is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern. Affected individuals carry biallelic mutations in the POLH gene.

checks.claim: XPV is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.
checks.evidence_quote: Xeroderma pigmentosum (XP) is an autosomal recessive disease characterized by a high incidence of skin cancers.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that XP in general is autosomal recessive, not XPV specifically.

checks.claim: Individuals affected with XPV carry biallelic mutations in the POLH gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We found that all XP-V cells examined carry mutations in their DNA polymerase eta gene.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports mutations but does not say they are biallelic.

paragraphs.text: Masutani et al. (1999) purified from HeLa cells a DNA polymerase that corrected the replication defect of XPV cell extracts and could bypass a thymine dimer accurately. They cloned the corresponding gene, a human homolog of yeast RAD30, which encodes DNA polymerase eta. They found truncating mutations in this gene in cells from XPV patients.

checks.claim: Masutani et al. (1999) purified from HeLa cells a DNA polymerase that corrected the replication defect of XPV cell extracts.
checks.evidence_quote: we have recently isolated a DNA polymerase from HeLa cells that continues replication on damaged DNA by bypassing ultraviolet-induced thymine dimers in XP-V cell extracts.
checks.explanation: The polymerase came from HeLa cells and restored thymine-dimer bypass in XP-V cell extracts.

checks.claim: The DNA polymerase purified by Masutani et al. (1999) from HeLa cells could bypass a thymine dimer accurately.
checks.evidence_quote: a DNA polymerase from HeLa cells that continues replication on damaged DNA by bypassing ultraviolet-induced thymine dimers
checks.explanation: The abstract confirms bypass of thymine dimers but says nothing about whether the bypass is accurate.

checks.claim: Masutani et al. (1999) cloned the gene encoding the purified polymerase, a human homolog of yeast RAD30 that encodes DNA polymerase eta.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we show that this polymerase is a human homologue of the yeast Rad30 protein, recently identified as DNA polymerase eta.
checks.explanation: The abstract identifies the polymerase as the human Rad30 homolog (pol eta). The mention of recombinant protein implies the gene was cloned.

checks.claim: Masutani et al. (1999) found truncating mutations in the DNA polymerase eta gene in cells from XPV patients.
checks.evidence_quote: We found that all XP-V cells examined carry mutations in their DNA polymerase eta gene.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports mutations in XP-V cells but does not say they were truncating.

paragraphs.text: Johnson et al. (1999) independently identified mutations in the human RAD30 homolog (POLH) in XPV cell lines.

checks.claim: Johnson et al. (1999) independently identified mutations in the human RAD30 homolog (POLH) in XPV cell lines.
checks.evidence_quote: Here it is shown that XP variant (XP-V) cell lines harbor nonsense or frameshift mutations in hRAD30, the human counterpart of yeast RAD30.
checks.explanation: The abstract directly reports hRAD30 mutations in XP-V cell lines.

paragraphs.text: Broughton et al. (2002) analyzed POLH in a larger series of XPV patients and found a variety of mutations. Most were nonsense, frameshift or splicing mutations predicted to give truncated or absent protein. A few were missense mutations within the polymerase domain.

checks.claim: Broughton et al. (2002) analyzed POLH in a larger series of XPV patients and found a variety of mutations.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 11 cited papers. This is Broughton et al. (2002); the Masutani abstract does not address it.

checks.claim: Most POLH mutations found by Broughton et al. (2002) in XPV patients were nonsense, frameshift or splicing mutations predicted to give truncated or absent protein.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 11 cited papers. This is Broughton et al. (2002); the Masutani abstract does not address it.

checks.claim: A few POLH mutations found by Broughton et al. (2002) in XPV patients were missense mutations within the polymerase domain.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 11 cited papers. This is Broughton et al. (2002); the Masutani abstract does not address it.

paragraphs.text: DNA polymerase eta copies past cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers relatively accurately, inserting adenines opposite the thymines of a thymine-thymine dimer. When it is absent, other more error-prone polymerases bypass the lesion instead. This is thought to cause the increased UV mutagenesis and skin cancer seen in XPV.

checks.claim: DNA polymerase eta copies past cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers relatively accurately.
checks.evidence_quote: Yeast RAD30 encodes a DNA polymerase involved in the error-free bypass of ultraviolet (UV) damage.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes error-free bypass of UV damage in general, and for the yeast protein. It does not mention cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers.

checks.claim: DNA polymerase eta inserts adenines opposite the thymines of a thymine-thymine dimer.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not say which nucleotides are inserted opposite the dimer.

checks.claim: When DNA polymerase eta is absent, other more error-prone polymerases bypass UV-induced lesions instead.
checks.evidence_quote: In the absence of poleta, Chk1 kinase becomes essential for replication resumption by alternative pathways, via fork stabilization.
checks.explanation: Abstract mentions alternative pathways in the absence of poleta but not error-prone polymerases bypassing lesions.

checks.claim: Bypass of UV lesions by error-prone polymerases in the absence of polymerase eta is thought to cause the increased UV mutagenesis and skin cancer seen in XPV.
checks.evidence_quote: they suggest that error-free replication of UV lesions by hRad30 plays an important role in minimizing the incidence of sunlight-induced skin cancers
checks.explanation: The abstract links the loss of error-free replication to skin cancer. It does not mention error-prone polymerases or UV mutagenesis.

paragraphs.text: Zeng et al. (2001) found an altered spectrum of somatic hypermutation in immunoglobulin genes from XPV patients, with fewer mutations at A/T base pairs. This suggested that polymerase eta takes part in somatic hypermutation.

checks.claim: Zeng et al. (2001) found an altered spectrum of somatic hypermutation in immunoglobulin genes from XPV patients, with fewer mutations at A/T base pairs.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 11 cited papers. This is Zeng et al. (2001); the Masutani abstract does not discuss somatic hypermutation.

checks.claim: The altered somatic hypermutation spectrum in XPV patients suggested that polymerase eta takes part in somatic hypermutation.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 11 cited papers. This is Zeng et al. (2001); the Masutani abstract does not discuss somatic hypermutation.

paragraphs.text: Mice deficient for Polh developed skin tumors after UV irradiation, which modeled the cancer susceptibility of XPV (Lin et al., 2006; Ohkumo et al., 2006).

checks.claim: Mice deficient for Polh developed skin tumors after UV irradiation (Lin et al., 2006; Ohkumo et al., 2006).
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 11 cited papers. This is Lin et al. and Ohkumo et al. (2006); the Masutani abstract does not mention mouse models.

checks.claim: UV-induced skin tumors in Polh-deficient mice modeled the cancer susceptibility of XPV.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 11 cited papers. The Masutani abstract does not mention mouse models.
